papers.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
papers.problem: Teams building practice apps for phone agents do not know which parts they can safely cut.
papers.fix: Rewarding only one reference path cut success by 10.53 points, while pruning unused features raised success from 51.61% to 56.13%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Keep the reward rules and app data complete, and cut unused features, to build cheaper training setups that work better.
papers.limitation: It tests one small model family, so the result may not hold for other models.

papers.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
papers.problem: Robot control models fail when objects move at different speeds, and few tests check this.
papers.fix: Six of eight models peaked at middle speeds, and adding past frames raised success by 10-40 points for three models.
papers.practicalUseCase: Feed your robot model recent past frames or a speed estimate, and test it at many speeds.
papers.limitation: The tests run in simulation on conveyor belts, so real robots may behave differently.

papers.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
papers.problem: Teaching a small visual agent usually needs many practice runs, and nobody knew how few would work.
papers.fix: Four recorded runs raised a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on Navigation and 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban.
papers.practicalUseCase: Train small agents on a few well-chosen recorded runs before you pay for more practice.
papers.limitation: It covers three puzzle-style tasks only, so other task types may need more experience.

papers.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
papers.problem: Robot agents built on language models forget past steps, misread why they failed, and waste what they learn.
papers.fix: A two-agent setup that rewrites its own guidance reached 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on benchmarks, and 96.7% in real tasks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Let a second agent turn failures into written guidance, so your robot improves without any retraining.
papers.limitation: The real-world test covers only three manipulation tasks.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still leave large groups out of formal finance, even as Islamic finance grows.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, tertiary education, institution quality, and internet access shaped inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital infrastructure, youth and female empowerment, and higher income matter most, so Islamic banks should aim products there.
papers.limitation: It shows links between country factors and inclusion, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collection stays low, and it was unclear whether better waqf knowledge changes how Muslims give.
papers.fix: In 642 Indonesian Muslims, waqf literacy raised attitude, social norms, control, and past behaviour, which lifted giving intent.
papers.practicalUseCase: Teach people what waqf is, because knowledge pushes giving up, so waqf groups should fund literacy work.
papers.limitation: It uses a survey of Muslims in Indonesia only, so it shows intent, not actual donations.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody had mapped how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what makes an issue large.
papers.fix: Of 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, social purposes, and USD or Euro currency gave larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers should use equity-based contracts and major currencies, and keep second party opinion costs low to raise issue size.
papers.limitation: It covers 2012 to 2022 issues only, and growth sits mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear whether online interest in halal products pulls Islamic financing up in Muslim countries.
papers.fix: Across 16 OIC countries from 2014 to 2023, halal search interest raised total financing, mainly through Murabaha and Ijarah.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks should expect demand to lead supply, so push simple Murabaha and Ijarah products when halal interest rises.
papers.limitation: Search volume only proxies awareness, and the effect on Mudarabah and Musharakah is weak.
